name: AMOS22 CT, unlabelled (ids 5000-6899) and labelled
what: AMOS, a large-scale abdominal multi-organ benchmark: its unlabelled CT parts and its labelled set, Zenodo records 7262757, 7295661 and 7262581; tier 1 of the anomaly harvest: all five archives fetched, 2,400 scans listed (1,900 and 500), of which the data platform counts 723 CTs, about two thirds being thicker than 3 mm, and 2,200 subjects qualifying, about 102.6 GB in the source's catalogue (NIfTI); the unlabelled part has no patient ids, so people against volumes is unknown, and 200 of the labelled CTs are AbdomenAtlas people
level_truth: the data platform records no level labels from the release; its own automatic level calls, which no radiologist has read, are kept apart under its anomaly_harvest folder

segmentations.masks: the labelled set's masks, inside the fetched amos22.zip; their structures are to confirm on the release's page
vertebra masks by TotalSegmentator and by SPINEPS with VERIDAH, each vertebra named by level, and the level call made from the two together
segmentations.by: the data platform's anomaly harvest, automatic; no radiologist has read them

how_to_get: spinesurg-ct-nnunet's slurm/acquisition_fetch.sh zenodo --collection amos22 --record 7262757 7295661 7262581 --include '(amos22_unlabeled_ct_[0-9_]+\.zip|amos22\.zip)$', submitted from the harvest's acquisition folder; the check is FETCH_STATUS.json's unresolved_failures at 0, and, by the manifest's note, 5 zips by md5 to verify.

The route as the manifest prints it: python3 data/reproduce/reacquire/reacquire.py --grid amos22; on the grid, from ~/spinesurg-ct-nnunet/data_platform/reacquire, sbatch -D "$PWD" --export=ALL,IDS="amos22",MODE=--run reacquire.sbatch, as a Slurm job on the owner's word.
